headline: US Supreme Court declines to hear appeal over order blocking federal research grant rescissions
dek: The American Thoracic Society said the court's decision is good news for researchers led by Neeta Thakur, MD, who challenged the rescission of grants for work including climate change and health equity.
body:
The US Supreme Court has chosen not to hear the Trump Administration's appeal against a temporary restraining order that blocks the rescission of certain federal research grants, the American Thoracic Society (ATS) said in a LinkedIn post.

According to ATS, Neeta Thakur, MD, a past chair of the ATS Health Equity and Diversity Committee and a researcher at UCSF, led a class action suit earlier this year. The suit challenged an attempt to rescind federal grants that did not meet "Administration priorities", including research on climate change and health equity. ATS said hundreds of researchers, including many of its members, found their federal grants at risk.

A federal court issued a temporary order blocking the Administration from rescinding the grant funding. ATS said Dr Thakur and her colleagues who filed the suit received further good news this week when the Supreme Court declined to hear the appeal.

Gary Ewart, ATS executive vice president of advocacy and government relations, said the temporary restraining order only provides relief to scientists in the University of California system. He added that the fact the court granted the initial relief, and that the Supreme Court chose to continue to block the Administration's efforts, "implies that the Administration is on very weak legal footing in its attempts to rescind research grant funding".

Mr Ewart said he hoped the court would continue to support the researcher community when it decides the underlying merits of the class action lawsuit.
key_quote: I hope the court continues to support the researcher community when it decides the underlying merits of the class action lawsuit.
